title: Ambrosian book states: bounded calendar and prayer revisions

traditions.label: Ambrosian Missal
traditions.scope: Historical and reformed Latin source states of Milan; independent translation history deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: Selective, non-exhaustive; dates attest publication/approval/effectiveness, never duration of validity. 1913 critical edition and 2026 publication do not become extra reforms. Research handoff for independent review: documented denotes source-described attestation, not checked transcription. Independent histories of the 1990 Italian update and 2008 lectionary are not represented as replacement missals; translation-only 2020 changes remain excluded.

sources.title: BnF FRBNF36814098: Missale ambrosianum duplex

sources.title: Jacopo Maria Calloni, La tradizione manoscritta del messale ambrosiano

sources.title: Uwe Michael Lang, Votive Masses of the Holy Face of Christ in Early Printed Diocesan Missals, Mediaeval Studies 79 (2017), 165–203
sources.inspection: Read rendered p. 169 and notes 12–13 identifying 1475/1499 formularies and the 1594 witness. Screenshot unavailable.
sources.limitations: Original comparative research, read in PDF text rendering; not independently checked against book images. Rationale for removal is expressly probable.

sources.title: Anthony Ward, Modern Ambrosian Prefaces of Saints: Points of Contact with the Roman Missal, Notitiae 32 (1996), 238–267
sources.inspection: Read pp. 239–244, 266–267 in rendered PDF; attempted images 62, 63, 87 failed.
sources.limitations: Exact Latin wording unverified; source-described changes only. Original altar books not collated. Publication in an official periodical does not turn scholarship into a decree. The present dossier was prepared from web-rendered text; no source text was acquired through the model or transcribed into this dossier.

stages.label: Approved postconciliar source
stages.scope: Reformed Latin texts approved 30 November 1974; attached exemplar unavailable.
stages.summary: Reform includes Roman-source and newly composed prayers.

evidence.claim: Approves reformed Latin source and describes enrichment.

stages.limitations: Approval is not a 1974 printed book or proof of word-for-word identity with 1981.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: First postconciliar Latin book
stages.scope: Published Latin source: selected Sanctoral prefaces described by Ward; calendar organization represented only through the official Latin publisher’s retrospective replacement-and-reorganization account, not a reconstructed calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Mediolani 1981, promulgated under Giovanni Colombo; Ward MA.

evidence.locus: Description: paragraph beginning La pubblicazione della II edizione latina and following principal-changes list, especially La riorganizzazione dell’anno liturgico
evidence.claim: Identifies the first Latin edition of 1981 as the book replaced and describes the successor’s reorganization into seasons after Epiphany and Pentecost. This supplies a retrospective predecessor-calendar scope, without individual 1981 assignments.

stages.limitations: Complete book unavailable in this lane. 1974 approved exemplar and 1975 confirmations not collated; no separate 1981 reform asserted. This publication and the 1974 approval must not be counted as two independently established substantive recensions. Calendar evidence is retrospective and structural only: no 1981 calendar page, feast assignment, Sunday count or precise intermediate source state has been inspected. The evidence does not transfer the Italian 1976/1990 calendar’s exact contents into the Latin 1981 book.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Second reformed source recension
stages.scope: Second Latin typical source and Italian expression; effective 17 November 2024.
stages.witness_label: Latin second typical text approved 7 December 2023; Italian 2024 ISBN 9788868946821; Latin 2026 ISBN 9788868948627.
stages.summary: Reorganized year, updated saints and expanded prayer repertory.

evidence.claim: Approves Latin source and Italian translation.
Associates 2026 Latin publication with second recension.

stages.limitations: 2026 is a publication witness, not a third source reform. Italian-only wording changes are excluded. No complete Latin 1981/2026 collation.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

evidence.claim: Latin successor replaces 1981 and receives structural/repertory changes.

transitions.limitations: Non-immediate comparison: 1990 update, 2008 lectionary, 2010 calendar and 2020 supplement require component histories. New-composition examples described for 2024 publication; Latin loci unverified. No translation-only Gloria/Pater Noster changes counted. Former Sunday count disputed 32/34. The calendar change is documented only at the structural level of this retrospective official account; no exact Latin 1981 calendar assignments or Sunday total are claimed.
